div.div: 4 اسنقهُ النَّعِيمُ i. q. تَرَّفَهُ [i. e. Ease and plenty caused him to exult, or to exult greatly, or excessively, and to behave insolently and unthankfully, or ungratefully: or wealth made him to enjoy, or lead, a plentiful, and a pleasant or an easy, and a soft or delicate, life; or a life of ease and plenty]. (O, K.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
